title: The spectrum functor on commutative Hopf algebras
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. A commutative Hopf $k$-algebra here means a unital commutative $k$-algebra $A$ with $k$-algebra maps $\Delta_A:A\to A\otimes_k A$, $\epsilon_A:A\to k$, $S_A:A\to A$ such that $(\Delta_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\Delta_A)\Delta_A$, $(\epsilon_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\epsilon_A)\Delta_A=1_A$, and $\mu_A(S_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=\mu_A(1\otimes S_A)\Delta_A=\eta_A\epsilon_A$, under the usual tensor unit and associativity identifications; $\mu_A$ and $\eta_A$ are multiplication and unit. Tensor products are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The assignment $A\mapsto\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is a contravariant functor from commutative Hopf $k$-algebras to affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme]: multiplication, identity and inverse are induced by $\Delta_A$, $\epsilon_A$ and $S_A$. For a $k$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$ preserving these three maps, $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a group-scheme homomorphism; identities and compositions are respected contravariantly.
